name: OPAL '7d' duration literal rejected
input_turn: Turns out OPAL rejects '7d' as a duration literal in filter expressions. The error 'expected duration literal' is misleading — it actually wants hours. So '7d' must be '168h', and '14d' must be '336h'. Verified by trying both forms in @"My Dataset".

name: Tracing/Span cascade-ordering deadlock
input_turn: Surprisingly, deleteDatastream on Tracing/Span fails because the managed datasets reference each other in a cycle. There's no force flag on any delete mutation. Worked around it by deleting the parent folder via deleteFolder, which cascades through. This deadlock pattern shows up on Kubernetes Explorer too.

name: observe -D flag emits raw GraphQL even on parse crash
input_turn: The Observe CLI has a -D debug flag that emits raw GraphQL request and response payloads to stderr, EVEN WHEN the CLI itself crashes parsing the result. That's how I extracted dataset metadata when 'observe list dataset' was panicking — the response was intact in the debug stream.

name: App uninstall does NOT cascade datasets
input_turn: Just learned that uninstalling an Observe app does not cascade-delete the datasets that app installed. The data is preserved over the metadata — datasets remain orphaned with no managedById link, and you have to delete them manually via the API. This is opposite from what you'd expect.

name: Non-Observe technical fact — REJECT
input_turn: Discovered that Python's subprocess.TimeoutExpired inherits from subprocess.SubprocessError, NOT from OSError or RuntimeError. So a `except OSError` clause won't catch it. This caused the observe-learning-capture plugin's classifier hook to crash silently on long Haiku calls. Important lesson but Python-specific, not Observe.

name: API error pattern — operational vs validation
input_turn: The Observe API mutations return errors in two distinct shapes. Validation errors (bad arguments, missing fields) come as a top-level `errors[]` array and are permanent — retrying with the same args won't help. Operational errors (dependency-blocked deletes, ownership conflicts) come as `errorMessage` inside `data.deleteX` with `success: false`, and these CAN succeed after their downstreams are removed. Distinguish in retry logic.
